title: One A Week
summary:
One A Week
For more than ten years now, a familiar lament in the Aframax sector has been that, "roughly one Aframax per week will deliver, how will the market absorb this amount of tonnage?" As shown below, Aframax deliveries have ranged from a low of 13 in 2001 to a high of 77 in 2003. The average of 40 is just below one per week. Rising Rates
The size of the orderbook has generally suggested a bearish picture for rates, yet earnings for Aframaxes have gotten progressively stronger over time.

children.title: Spot Market Action
children.summary: The total amount of reported spot market activity has been on the rise overall for the past ten years and has declined somewhat in the past three. The total number of reported fixtures was 3,866 in 1996 and peaked in 2002 at 5,283, as indicated by the chart on the next page.

children.title: Up Doesn't Mean Down
children.summary: The theory that the increase in fleet will lead to a decline in rates has certainly not proven itself in the Aframax sector. The increasing demand for tonnage has outpaced the orderbook and contributed to a positive rate trend over the past ten years.
